title.narrative: Water for Women Climate Resilient Inclusive Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) Fund (2018-2025)

description.narrative: Funding under this investment (2018-2025; $159.9 million) has supported improved sustainable access to climate resilient inclusive water, sanitation and hygiene services in 16 Asia Pacific countries. The initiative follows input from the High-Level Panel for Water in New York and the Civil Society WASH Fund. In its second phase (project implementation from January 2023 - December 2024), the Fund is partnering with eight Civil Society Organisations (CSOs) to implement 15 WASH projects with the aim of improving the delivery of inclusive climate-resilient WASH. Research remains an important focus, with four research partners undertaking seven new research projects with the aim of addressing knowledge and practice gaps for climate-resilient, inclusive WASH. To date, the Fund has supported more than 3.7 million people, including the most marginalised in communities.

Climate adaptation, mitigation, environment and biodiversity

description.narrative: Bhutan is the world’s first carbon negative country. Its fragile ecosystem within the Himalayas makes it highly vulnerable to monsoon rains, increased snow melts, landslides, glacial lake floods, and changing river patterns and water availability. ‍ ‍Some 35 percent of Bhutan’s water sources are drying up, and more than 30 percent of the population report water security as their greatest concern. Despite this, most rural areas lack risk management systems (via water safety plans) to support the delivery of quality water from source to tap. ‍ ‍Water for Women, through the Dutch NGO, SNV and University of Technology Sydney - Institute for Sustainable Futures, is working with local communities, government and water supply operators in rural Bhutan to improve access to reliable, climate-resilient water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services. ‍ ‍The project has strengthened capacities to adapt rural WASH services, systems, plans, and budgets, including by addressing the increasing vulnerabilities of disadvantaged groups in accessing climate-resilient, inclusive WASH.

description.narrative: Despite being the world’s first carbon negative country, Bhutan’s fragile ecosystem within the Himalayas makes it highly vulnerable to monsoon rains, increased snow melts, landslides, glacial lake outburst floods, and changing patterns of river discharge and water availability. ‍ Some 35 percent of Bhutan’s water sources are reportedly drying up, and water security is considered the greatest concern for more than 30 percent of the population. Despite this, most rural water schemes lack water safety plans and water management arrangements are limited. ‍ Water for Women, through SNV and University of Technology Sydney - Institute for Sustainable Futures, is working with local communities, government and water supply operators in rural Bhutan to improve access to reliable, climate-resilient water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services. ‍ The project is strengthening adaptive capacities within rural WASH services, systems, plans, and budgets, including addressing the increasing vulnerabilities of disadvantaged groups in accessing climate-resilient, inclusive WASH solutions.

description.narrative: Through Water for Women research projects in the Pacific, the International WaterCentre at Griffith University (IWC) has been working with government, civil society and universities to co-develop more effective and transformative community water management approaches. In rural Fiji, Solomon Islands and Vanuatu, sustainable water committees play a crucial role in community-based water management and water security. IWC’s research leverages formal, informal and emergent social networks to allow key stakeholders to better understand, plan for and respond to climate change risks and impacts on inclusive water and WASH in their communities. Through these efforts, IWC’s research has helped to strengthen water committees and promote climate-resilient water management and inclusive WASH practices in these countries. Based on successes from this work, IWC is currently co-designing a new community-based water security planning approach with the Government of Fiji.

title.narrative: Climate adaptation, mitigation, environment and biodiversity

description.narrative: Water for Women is strengthening the climate resilience of water resource, and water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) systems and access to services in Nusa Tenggara Timur (NTT) and Nusa Tenggara Barat (NTB) in Indonesia. Both NTT and NTB are highly vulnerable to extreme weather events, sea-level rises and increasing temperatures. These hazards directly impact agriculture, health, education, and are predicted to drive income loss per capita to 5 percent by 2050. ‍ Through an integrated approach to water management (involving the provincial government, private sector, community organisations, Monash University and Plan International), the project has supported: development of a coastal revitalisation program for Sumbawa, including planting 120,000 mangrove seedlings to mitigate seawater encroachment and coastal erosion. It has also provided targeted support to government to strengthen the climate resilience of Sumbawa’s Long Term Development Plan, new district regulation on water resource protection, and implementation of community-based total sanitation processes.
